title: Processing and characterization of flame-retardant natural fibre-reinforced epoxy composites and construction of selection charts for engineering applications
source_version: Published original article, volume18 issue8 pages779–795
source_material_form_TGA_raw: JFREC with FR, corresponding composite labels in Table 5;5–10 mg specimen
source_material_form_LOI_raw: Jute/epoxy composites, same labels in Table 4; dimensions not separately reported
TGA_specimen_preparation: Aliquot of corresponding cured composite,5–10 mg; cutting/grinding, pan, gas flow, conditioning and repetitions unreported.
LOI_specimen_preparation: Corresponding composite labels in Table 4; instrument, specimen dimensions, mounting, conditioning, repeat count and uncertainty unreported. Mechanical-test dimensions and n=8 are not transferred.
TG_locator: Original p789 Table 5 composite rows; p784 TGA method defines onset at 5% loss and maximum decomposition-rate temperature; Figure 9 ordinate derivative weight[%/C]
LOI_locator: Original p786 Table 4; own test results Section 3.3 pp786–787
source_location: Original pp783–784 preparation and Tables2/3; p786 Table 4; p789 Table 5 and Figures8/9
pairing_evidence: Tables3,4 and5 use identical prepared composite codes for the sole six-ply jute-fabric laminate preparation; separate pure epoxy and free-jute rows in Table 5 are excluded. FR is applied either to the epoxy matrix or to the jute reinforcement, and the routes remain distinct.
source_fabric_thread_count: 5 threads/cm in both warp and weft
source_resin_hardener_ratio: Biresin CR82-6:Biresin CH80-6=100:27 by weight, Table2
source_vacuum_statement: 100 kPa (absolute) under vacuum, as printed; actual pressure interpretation unresolved
source_peak_caption: Figure 9 and Table 5 say DTA; plotted ordinate is derivative weight[%/C] and method/prose explicitly describe maximum decomposition rate and DTG. Preserve original caption wording.
washing_state: Initial cured laminate; no durability washing assigned
limitations: Only five internally consistent treated laminate states are retained. Untreated UJE is held for LOI 21 in prose versus 21.8 in Table 4. UJ18DE is held for Table 4 LOI 26.8 versus 35.5 in the adjacent prose and conclusion. Table 1 and Figure 13 include literature values and are not independent observations from this source. Pure epoxy and free-jute thermal rows lack matching own LOI and are excluded. Source Table 3 text-layer extraction falsely appends zeros to18/27/54; actual original table pixels show18,27,54 and are used without changing printed values. DAP percentages in Table 3 are reported on different named bases (jute, epoxy, whole composite); no denominator conversion is inferred. All composite fabric contents are given only as23–26 wt%, not exact per row. Six-ply vacuum-bagging and overnight cure followed by60 °C/6 h postcure apply to the paired composites. The reported vacuum 100 kPa absolute is retained without correction. T5 is explicitly 5% mass loss, not a tangent onset; Tonset is blank. The source first/second/third step peaks preserve their original stage order. The DTA caption is inconsistent with the plotted derivative-weight axis and explicit DTG/max-rate method; no differential-thermal peak is borrowed. No graphical coordinate estimation, arithmetic residue conversion or mechanical/VFT dimensions/replication transfer is used. Figure 1 shows80 °C oven drying of DAP-treated fabric whereas Section 2.2 states70 °C; the actual treated-fabric drying temperature is unresolved and both statements are preserved. Specimen history is paired by explicit laminate labels, with this preparation limitation disclosed.
sample_state: UJ3DE; six-ply jute/epoxy laminate; FRM DAP route; initial cured state
treatment_method: DAP powder nominal 3% in epoxy (Table 3 basis), untreated-for-DAP jute reinforcement; declared total-composite DAP 2.25%. Powder mixing time/temperature and specific pretreatment history of the untreated reinforcement are not separately reported. Six 235 g/m² plain-woven jute plies270 × 200 mm; epoxy CR82-6/CH80-6 resin/hardener100:27 by weight. Hand lay-up followed by vacuum bagging at source-reported 100 kPa absolute, overnight cure and 60 °C postcure 6 h. Fabric fraction 23–26 wt%, exact row value unreported.
